In such case, a new technology assistance is required to provide a novel support to physicians as well as guardians to know about their respective individual's health details in clear manner. The concept of Internet of Things (IoT) is used to identify the patient or respective individual such as elder people's health conditions instantly and record those details into the remote cloud server. The proposed application is designed with the help of multiple intelligent health assisted sensors such as Pressure Sensor, Temperature Sensor and the Heartbeat identification sensor. Those individuals who are unable to go to a clinic quickly might benefit from remote patient surveillance. Because of its ability to detect illness and provide targeted treatment, IoT holds great promise for improving care for the elderly and expanding access to healthcare in underserved areas. Small, wireless devices that may be worn by patients to track vitals are known as Wireless Healthcare Networks. This study utilizes a Rivest Shamir Adleman (RSA) security norms to the proposed health monitoring scheme and it is a rating for how effectively the respective healthcare gadget can pick up the signal from a WiFi connection or wireless device. The primary concept is to allow the doctor to safely obtain patient data by distributing secret keys produced using the RSA method used by the remote database to a public key produced among multiple entities.

articleTitle: A Robust Deep Neural Network Framework for the Detection of Dementia
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Social Networking (ICPCSN)
abstract: The basic goal of this Deep Learning (DL) framework is to identify early pathological signals that people could miss in order to improve physicians' effectiveness in disease identification. The most common degenerative condition that causes dementia, is the Alzheimer's disease (AD), it offers serious health hazards to middle aged and older people. Different people can experience dementia in different ways and it will create individual signs dependent on the fragment of their brain which is affected. However, it is more essential to treat this disease because, the person with this disease may suffer to communicate with others, to eat and chew their own food etc. Several state-of-art methods are utilized for the detection of dementia earlier. In this study, the detection of dementia is done by DL based Convolutional Neural Network (CNN). The Grey Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) is recycled for the feature extraction process. The Spider Monkey Optimization (SMO) is used in this study for feature selection process. Subsequently, CNN is a deep learning (DL) network architecture that it will learn directly from the data. This will be utilized for identifying objects and the category of the image pattern. Moreover, this can also be used for signaling the data, time-series and categorizing signal. Therefore, the investigational outcome reveals that the future algorithm has the ability to identify and treat dementia. The effectiveness of the proposed work can be proved by comparing the CNN with other existing models. The comparison outcome gives the proposed system has better accuracy than other existing methods.

articleTitle: A Review on Blockchain Based Security in Education
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Social Networking (ICPCSN)
abstract: Blockchain technology is very well positioned, and the education industry may greatly benefit from blockchain technology, which can be used for digital credentials, academic records, learning management systems, funding and payments, research, and collaboration. The development of distributed registries in blockchain technology is employed in educational institutions to provide digital credentials. Learning platforms built on the blockchain can offer individualized learning experiences by monitoring student progress and adapting the content to suit each student's requirements. This study examined the use of blockchain in academic institutions through a review of the literature. It aims to examine the difficulties encountered by educational organizations while deploying an innovative application that provides unchangeable, trustworthy records of students' lifelong learning. Implementing blockchain to address educational obstacles like scalability, integrity, privacy, and security problems. The most problematic and contentious issues relating to blockchain security, challenges, and legislation have been discussed in detail. For blockchain technology to be implemented by higher education as a digital technology, this study offers a translucent exploration of blockchain.

articleTitle: Food and Beverage Handling System with Automated Controls
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Social Networking (ICPCSN)

articleTitle: An IoT Based Mitigation of Occupational Dust Risks in Glass Manufacturing Plants
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Social Networking (ICPCSN)
abstract: The production of glass in the industrial setting can have both positive and negative impacts on people, with occupational dust posing a significant health risk to workers. This research study proposes an Internet of Things (IoT) based solution for mitigating occupational dust risks in glass manufacturing plants. The solution integrates various sensors, including temperature, gas, pressure, optical, and vibration sensors, to monitor the working environment in real-time and alert workers and management of any potential safety hazards. The data collected from these sensors is analyzed using advanced algorithms to optimize the glass production process and reduce waste. The solution also helps to improve worker safety by reducing exposure to occupational dust and other harmful substances. Results from the study show that the proposed IoT solution has the potential to significantly reduce occupational dust risks in glass manufacturing plants, while also improving the efficiency and sustainability of the production process. This study highlights the importance of incorporating IoT technologies in the glass industry to promote a safe and sustainable working environment.

articleTitle: Crop Prediction using Machine Learning Techniques and IoT
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Social Networking (ICPCSN)
abstract: Agriculture being the backbone of the Indian economy faces multiple challenges in the production of quality food and good yield due to the unnatural climatic changes, which reduces crop yield adversely. Farmers lack the knowledge to forecast the future crop yield and take the necessary precautions. Therefore, this research aims to assist farmers in crop selection by predicting suitable crops for a given region using supervised machine learning algorithms. The work focusses on achieving the improved accuracy of crop prediction when compared to the existing models. Seed data with the appropriate parameters such as humidity, soil pH, temperature, rainfall, nitrogen, potassium, and phosphorus content are collected to support its maximum growth. Based on the obtained data, the crop prediction is performed. Performance of the Naïve Bayes Classifier, Ada Boost Classifier, Decision Tree Classification, and Voting Classifier algorithms are compared based on the accuracy, confusion matrix, and other performance metrics like precision, recall, and F1 score. The Decision Tree classifier algorithm is chosen as the best algorithm for crop prediction and the model is hence deployed with it. The finest accuracy of around 99.4 % is achieved by the proposed model.

articleTitle: Image Understanding of GUI Widgets for Test Reuse
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Social Networking (ICPCSN)
abstract: Testing of UI after its development is an essential activity. Due to the complexity of the task of developing new tests for UI, it is an expensive one. Different approaches for reusing tests in similar scenarios have been created. These different methods employ different information available in the GUI to decide the appropriate transfer of tests from one UI to another. Similar GUI events are related together by these systems to decide the transferability of tests. The usage of semantic knowledge during the matching of GUI events has proven to be an important asset in understanding their similarities. The usage of textual information available in GUI and their semantic meanings in this task have promising results. However, the usage of semantic information that can be obtained from images and icons has remained unexplored. This study presents the integration of semantic annotation of icons, widgets and images for semantic matching of GUI events. Proposed findings demonstrate the importance of image understanding of GUI widgets in test reuse and offer practical insights for software developers and researchers. In addition to improving semantic matching, the integration of semantic annotation of icons, widgets, and images can also enhance the interpretability and maintainability of UI tests.

articleTitle: Multimodal Approach for Detecting Depression Using Physiological and Behavioural Data
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Social Networking (ICPCSN)
abstract: Depression is a widespread mental illness that can have a significant impact on an individual's overall well-being. Therefore, the use of depression detection systems has become increasingly crucial in identifying and assessing the presence and severity of depression in various settings, such as primary care offices, mental health clinics, and online platforms. In the past, depression detection was typically performed through clinical interviews, where psychologists would evaluate the subject's responses to determine their mental state. In this study, a model has been developed that combines three modalities - text, audio, and video - to predict the patient's mental health status. The output is classified into different levels to consider the subject's level of depression. This fusion approach is designed to address several issues, such as handling noise in one modality and controlling the contribution level of a specific modality, to provide a more accurate and comprehensive assessment of a patient's mental state.

articleTitle: Fully Automated Pothole Detection and Repair System using Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Social Networking (ICPCSN)
abstract: India has many areas with poorly maintained roadways. In addition to causing physical problems like back discomfort and injured spines, potholes and uneven roadways can harm automobiles. This work demonstrates a completely autonomous robot that can identify and fix roads overnight at the lowest possible cost utilizing a high accuracy machine learning algorithm. The suggested model makes use of YOLO framework models, which have the highest (Placeholder1) accuracy according to MENG YANG (2020). The testing information is gathered from different automobiles across the nation. To increase the robot's accuracy, the hardware for the system makes use of various sensors that collect inputs and cross-validate the findings. The robot uses LIDAR, IMU, and ultrasonic sensors to determine the depth of potholes and identify structural problems on roads. The suggested model can reduce the cost of fixing a road by 60%.

articleTitle: IoT-Enabled Waste Reduction and Recycling to Alleviate Environmental Hazards
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Social Networking (ICPCSN)
abstract: The rapid pace of urbanization and industrialization has resulted in an alarming increase in the amount of construction and demolition (C&D) waste generated globally. This waste not only occupies a considerable amount of landfills but also causes severe environmental hazards. In this context, IoT-based waste management is emerging as a promising solution for reducing the amount of waste generated and mitigating environmental hazards. This paper proposes an IoT-enabled waste reduction and recycling approach specifically designed for the C&D sector. The proposed approach incorporates weight sensors, motion sensors, and fill level sensors to facilitate efficient waste management. Weight sensors are used to measure the weight of waste materials in real-time, while motion sensors detect the movement of waste materials during transportation and disposal. Fill level sensors are used to monitor the level of waste materials in waste containers and to optimize waste collection routes. The collected data from the sensors is processed in real-time through an IoT platform that provides comprehensive waste management analytics. The proposed system also includes a waste sorting module that utilizes image processing techniques to identify and sort different types of waste materials. The sorted waste materials can then be reused, recycled, or sold to secondary markets. The implementation of the proposed approach will result in reduced waste generation, increased waste recycling, and improved environmental conditions. Moreover, the proposed system is designed to be scalable and can be deployed in different regions to address local waste management challenges. Overall, this study demonstrates the potential of IoT-based waste management approaches for reducing environmental hazards caused by construction and demolition waste.

articleTitle: PREDICARE: Machine Learning Based Disease Diagnosis System
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Social Networking (ICPCSN)
abstract: Maintaining good physical, social, and mental health is vital for leading a fulfilling life. Early detection and treatment of illnesses are essential in preventing disease progression. To this end, this research study proposes an end-to-end solution that involves regularly monitoring symptoms and utilizing two major models for disease analysis and heart disease prediction. The study applies K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), XGBoost and Random Forest Classifier models to predict diseases at an early stage. Heart disease is a leading cause of death globally, and the study examines heart-related issues through Machine Learning (ML) based severity prediction model. This research study emphasizes the importance of early detection and offers a promising solution for preventing disease progression and improving overall health outcomes.

articleTitle: TOPSIS-based Feature Selection for Text Classifcation
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Social Networking (ICPCSN)
abstract: For the classification of huge amount of textual data we need to classify them for the purpose of information retrieval, document classification, spam filtering and so on. To apply machine learning algorithms we need to extract the features from the text data in the numeric format which becomes huge in size. To select the most accurate features from the whole dataset having high relevancy and less redundancy feature selection becomes an important part. This paper proposes a method based on “Multi Criteria Decision Making (MCDM)” for the purpose of feature selection and then we have applied multinomial naive bayes classifier with the integration of some of the similarity measures and validated our method with three different datasets. The results that we get outstands pre existing methods, we get better classification accuracy with our method three different datasets. Our method outperformed some of the baseline methods.

articleTitle: Expression of Concern for: Study of Natural Language Processing for Sentiment Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 3rd International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Social Networking (ICPCSN)
abstract: The study of opinions, sentiments, assessments, perspectives, and feelings as they are expressed in written language is the focus of sentiment analysis and evaluation mining. It is commonly the subject of text mining, information mining, and web mining because it is one of the most active study fields in natural language processing. Sentiment analysis has been applied in many different contexts, including the study of how events affect unofficial groups and the exploration of presumptions about goods and services. The importance of sentiment analysis is increasing at the same time as virtual entertainment such as surveys, group chats, web blogs, micro sites, Twitter, and interpersonal organizations. In this work, we provide the results of our preliminary studies on twitter sentiment analysis. This study seeks to distinguish subjects from sentiment in tweets. It recognizes the sentiment that refers to the particular problem using Natural Language Processing techniques. Our analysis consists of three main processes, subjective grouping, semantic affiliation, and extreme order, to characterize sentiment. By describing the syntactic relationship between sentiment dictionaries and subject, the study makes use of sentiment vocabularies. Exploratory results demonstrate that the proposed framework performs better than existing message sentiment analysis tools because tweets don't have the same architecture as traditional messages.
